title: Universal finite normal replacement of a single approximation stage
statement: Let S be a quasi-compact quasi-separated integral scheme with integrally closed stalks and N a Noetherian approximation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system]. For each i there are an integral scheme X with integrally closed stalks, a dominant alpha:S -> X and finite p:X -> N_i with alpha followed by p the projection. For any integral normal Y, dominant beta:S -> Y and g:Y -> N_i whose composite with beta is that projection, there is a unique f:Y -> X with beta followed by f equal to alpha and f followed by p equal to g. No diagram or transition maps are asserted.

source.place: Tag 0EZJ normal approximation paragraph; Tags 035E, 035N, 035L, 035Q (normalization universal property), 0335

proof.text: Let t:S -> N_i be the projection. It is quasi-compact since S is compact and N_i quasi-separated. Set Z=t.image, the concrete scheme-theoretic image. The scheme-theoretically dominant t.toImage descends reducedness from S; its dense range descends irreducibility. Thus Z is integral. Its closed immersion into N_i makes it locally of finite type over the integers.

Set X=Z.normalization, the existing absolute normalization in K(Z). The relative-normalization instance gives integrality, and the source-library normal-stalk theorem applied to Spec K(Z) gives normality. For finiteness, over a nonempty affine U of Z the preimage in Spec K(Z) is top. Its sections therefore identify with K(Z), the fraction field of A=Gamma(Z,U). Local finite type over ULift Z gives finite type over Z. Apply finiteTypeZDomain_integralClosure_finite and transfer finiteness along mapIntegralClosure. Apply isFinite_fromNormalization_of_finite and compose with the closed immersion Z -> N_i.
Apply dominant lifting to t.toImage:S -> Z to obtain dominant alpha:S -> X. Its composition with p=Z.fromNormalization;t.imageι is t.

For Y,beta,g in the universal property, beta is scheme-theoretically dominant because Y is reduced. Kernel invariance under precomposition gives ker(t)=ker(g), so IsClosedImmersion.lift factors g through Z. Cancel Z -> N_i to obtain beta;gZ=t.toImage; hence gZ is dominant. Lift gZ through normalization. Uniqueness gives beta;f=alpha, and composition gives f;p=g. Any other compatible f-prime is dominant since beta;f-prime=alpha. Cancelling Z -> N_i reduces uniqueness to uniqueness of the dominant lift of gZ.

proof_origin.note: D2 implements image normalization with proved private chart-finiteness and image-integrality helpers and a proved general dominant-lifting module. No new sorry.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_normal_finite_stage_universal {S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace S]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsIntegral S]
    (hS : ∀ x : S, IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x))
    (N : S.NoetherianApproximation) (i : N.I) :
    ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (α : S ⟶ X) (p : X ⟶ N.D.obj i),
      α ≫ p = N.π.app i ∧ IsFinite p ∧ IsDominant α ∧ IsIntegral X ∧
      (∀ x : X, IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
      (∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsIntegral Y)
        (_ : ∀ y : Y, IsIntegrallyClosed (Y.presheaf.stalk y))
        (β : S ⟶ Y) (_ : IsDominant β) (g : Y ⟶ N.D.obj i),
        β ≫ g = N.π.app i → ∃! f : Y ⟶ X, β ≫ f = α ∧ f ≫ p = g)
